leading_positions.synthesis: Three of eight members prefer targeted protein degradation as a single-topic prize and all three name Crews, Deshaies and Handa. They share the framing of induced proximity as a design principle that converts a ligand into an adaptor between an E3 ligase and a chosen protein, and they agree the mechanism is independently reproduced. They differ in emphasis: Aili stresses the modality shift from occupancy to event-driven pharmacology, Chabes the tool value for biologists and the genome-maintenance link, Linke the new capability and a coherent story for a broad audience. All three concede that no degrader drug is approved yet and that Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto, Kim and Ito are left out; Linke and Chabes also flag that Handa anchors the molecular-glue strand rather than the PROTAC concept, and Linke has not resolved whether Ciulli should replace Handa.

Two members prefer palladium-catalysed C-N cross-coupling for Buchwald and Hartwig. They share the view that attribution is the cleanest on the shortlist, that the method is ubiquitous in medicinal and process chemistry, and that maturity is not a concern. Both identify the 2010 cross-coupling prize as the main objection and note Kosugi's earlier tin-amide work as a precursor. Zou adds that a method rather than a new concept may struggle to reach five votes; Somfai notes the allocation awkwardness with Hartwig's other work.

One member prefers massively parallel sequencing by synthesis for Balasubramanian and Klenerman, on grounds of proven impact, overdue recognition and compact Cambridge attribution. He acknowledges that credit is contested with Rothberg, Mayer and Ju and that the field may be judged technology or medicine. Chabes would add Rothberg as a third name; B057 is also a listed alternative for Aili, Brzezinski and Linke, but that is not a first preference.

One member prefers long-range electron transfer through proteins for Gray and Winkler, citing a physically stated mechanism, four decades of confirmation and a compact attribution. He states that no other member ranked it in the opening, and he flags the overlap with Marcus theory (1992) and Dutton-Moser and Beratan-Onuchic priority.

One member proposes a two-part prize: phase separation for Hyman and Brangwynne, and ionizable lipid nanoparticles for Cullis alone. She rates the first part least mature, with contested physiological relevance, and the second as diffuse in credit; she notes that Rosen, Pappu and Mittag are dropped and that naming Cullis alone excludes Hope, Madden, MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer. No other member prefers either part.

areas_of_agreement: No candidate has majority support: the eight first preferences split 3 (B066), 2 (B038), 1 (B057), 1 (B023) and 1 (B036 with B015), and a majority requires five.
All eight members state that no specific conflict requires recusal.
Members distinguish chemical validation from clinical validation for B066, and confirmation by many independent groups is treated as the key maturity test across candidates.
Attribution within the three-name limit is acknowledged by supporters as the main weakness of B066, B057, B036/B015 and, to a lesser degree, B038.
B066, B057 and B038 recur as alternatives across members' configurations, so they form the practical field for round 2.
scientific_disputes: Whether B057 sequencing is a chemical achievement (reversible-terminator chemistry, surface attachment, fluorescence detection) or enabling platform technology or medicine; raised by Aqvist, Chabes, Aili and Brzezinski.

Whether C-N coupling (B038) is a new general capability or a heteroatom extension of the 2010 cross-coupling prize; Somfai and Zou argue distinctness, Aili questions how much it opens that chemists could not do before.

Whether biomolecular phase separation (B036) is established physical chemistry given the dispute over whether in vitro droplets reflect physiological condensates and assay artefacts; Sparr concedes this, Aili and Brzezinski rank it lower on that basis.
Whether the PROTAC and molecular-glue strands of B066 are one principle or two achievements within one citation.
attribution_disputes: B066: Crews, Deshaies and Handa are named by all three supporters, but Ciulli (VHL ligands, structure), Gray, Sakamoto and Kim (first PROTAC) and Ito have claims; Aqvist proposed Ciulli in place of Handa in the opening.
B057: Balasubramanian and Klenerman (Aqvist) against adding Rothberg (Chabes), with Mayer and Ju also credited on the ballot.
B038: Buchwald and Hartwig are agreed by Somfai and Zou, but Kosugi (and Migita) priority is unresolved and Zou asks whether it needs mention.
B036 and B015: Hyman and Brangwynne without Rosen, Pappu or Mittag; Cullis alone without Hope, Madden, MacLachlan, Anderson or Langer.
B023: Gray and Winkler against Dutton and Moser and Beratan and Onuchic priority claims.
maturity_disputes: B066 has no approved degrader drug; Aili and Linke would treat the confirmed mechanism as sufficient, whereas Chabes calls it possibly one or a few years early, and Zou and Aqvist raised the timing concern in the opening.
B036 is judged least mature by its own proposer because of the contested in vivo relevance.
B057, B038 and B023 are described as fully mature, so the contrast between overdue recognition and early recognition is a live question.
Whether the 2020 CRISPR prize makes B022 redundant and whether the 2023 Medicine prize on mRNA weakens a delivery-chemistry prize (Sparr).
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Brzezinski discloses a field affinity with B023 through bioenergetics and electron transfer but no tie to Gray or Winkler.
Aqvist discloses a possible bias toward computational work (B029 is his second alternative), with no tie to a candidate.
Chabes discloses topical overlap with nucleic-acid chemistry relevant to B057 and B022, without any tie to a candidate.
Sparr discloses professional closeness to the lipid and phase-separation literature (B015, B036) but no tie requiring recusal.
Collegial links disclosed without any link to a candidate: Zou with Secretary Brzezinski at Stockholm University, and Linke, Somfai and Sparr as Lund colleagues.
questions_for_round2: Will members who rank B066 first accept recognition before the first approved degrader, and what evidence short of approval (ternary-complex structures, thalidomide-class glues in medical use, late-stage trials) is sufficient?
For B066, who should hold the three places among Crews, Deshaies, Handa, Ciulli and Gray, and should the citation name PROTACs, molecular glues or both?

Does the 2010 cross-coupling prize cover C-N coupling, and if not, can supporters of B038 state what Buchwald and Hartwig enabled that the 2010 laureates did not, and how Kosugi's priority is treated?
Is massively parallel sequencing (B057) chemistry for this prize, and if so, does a defensible citation need a third name (Rothberg, Mayer or Ju), and on what priority evidence?
Can supporters of B023 and B036/B015 say whether their preferences would carry to B066, B038 or B057 as a second choice, given that each currently has a single supporter?
Would a two-part prize (as Linke raised, for example B066 with B022 or B057) or a single-topic prize be preferred, and could a combination reach five votes?
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 shows a split committee with no first preference above three votes. B066 leads narrowly and is most often named as an alternative, B038 has a compact two-member bloc with the cleanest attribution, and B057 is the most frequently cited mature alternative. The decisive questions concern timing and attribution for B066, scope relative to the 2010 prize for B038, and whether B057 counts as chemistry. Only positions explicit in the eight round-1 files are counted here.
